pr_title: Fix "muted" mod metronome not playing when expected
pr_body:
- [x] Depends on #14096 (for initial track volume and metronome transforms)

Closes #14090 

Also additionally clarifies in tooltip that `MuteComboCount = 0` mutes player audio completely.

issue_context.title: "Mute" metronome audio mutes on miss
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** "Mute" metronome audio disappear on miss then reappear on unknown reason (Known reason is when track end or fail. but during map is still unknown.). This also effect replay as well.

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7066150/127756042-3d667fff-8deb-4328-9419-30ab561bbf73.mp4

Replay : https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cNpRRfkkudA2krPujn10XUCTfLJIo4NR/view?usp=sharing

Mod : HD + Mute (Final volume at combo 0)
Map : https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/1311371#osu/2868033

**osu!lazer version:** 2021.731.0-lazer
comments: it’s supposed to silence on miss. that’s part of the mod?

If I understand this issue correctly, it's showing that the metronome silences when the player misses on "muted" with zero final combo. I believe on this case, it is expected for the metronome to play forever and the track to be silenced forever.

review_comments: Either this should be bypassed or (more correctly, if feasible) the inverse option should be set to false and disabled when the final volume combo is zero.

Disabling it may not work exactly with `Mod.CopyFrom` as it could potentially transfer a value while the bindable is disabled (see https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/issues/3218).

One other way to go with this however is changing the limits of the mute combo count to minimum 1 on the inverse option, which would also work with `Mod.CopyFrom` given that it does a full bind which transfers the limits as well. (I didn't notice that previously, which is the reason I've left this area alone)

I'm not convinced that this is going to work 100% correctly with `CopyFrom()`. Whether it will depends on the order of property binding I believe.

Consider:
```csharp
var mod = new MutedMod { InverseMuting = { Value = true }, MuteComboCount = { Value = 100 } };
mod.CopyFrom(new MutedMod { InverseMuting = { Value = false }, MuteComboCount = { Value = 0 } };
```

If `CopyFrom` transfers `InverseMuting` first then the copy will work correctly. If it doesn't, it won't. This needs to be unit tested.

I was aware of this at first, but it actually doesn't matter, since it binds the setting to the target setting and then unbinds from it, copying both the value and the defined limits.

I'll write a unit test for this as it could unintentionally break.
